subject.title: [Feature]: Support for Custom Emojis in Latest Telegram Bot API Update

question: What public API shape should OpenClaw expose for Telegram custom emoji entities in shared message-tool sends, captions, edits, and replies?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but raw Telegram entity arrays, Telegram-specific channel data, and a portable custom-emoji rich-text span would each change the shared message-tool/plugin boundary differently.

options.title: Define entity-bearing message API
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved entity representation and implement it consistently through message-tool, Telegram send/edit/caption/reply delivery, docs, and regression tests.

options.title: Keep rich HTML only
options.body: Treat `<tg-emoji>` HTML and opt-in rich messages as the supported path and leave user-supplied entity arrays unsupported.

options.title: Split design first
options.body: Create or designate a narrower API-design item before implementation so a future PR does not guess the permanent plugin contract.

recommendation.title: Define entity-bearing message API
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-approved entity representation and implement it consistently through message-tool, Telegram send/edit/caption/reply delivery, docs, and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest issue-thread and message-tool history signal for the public API-shape decision.
